hints: Sort movies by ending time and assign each movie to a member who is free by its start.
Among available members, choose the one whose previous movie ends latest; that preserves earlier-free members for future movies.
If no member is free, skip the movie.
analogy: Reserve the most recently freed compatible viewer, leaving the longest-free viewer available for tighter schedules.
example: With two members, movies [1,5),[2,5),[3,6),[6,9): the first two run together, then [6,9) follows one, for three movies.
algorithm: Sort intervals by finish time. Keep a multiset of member availability times; for a movie starting s, take the greatest finish<=s, replace it with its end, or skip if none.
correctness: Choosing the latest compatible availability leaves all other available members no worse for later movies; earliest finishing order maximizes opportunities for subsequent intervals.
complexity: O(n log n + n log k) time and O(k) availability space.
